Round of 16 opponents seem to be very varied in the new 48 team World Cup Just the way the draw is structured - some teams who win their group get a 3rd place team in the last 32 but a group winner in the last 16. Where others get 2nd place teams in both the last 32 and 16.  For instance France if they win their group play a 3rd place team in the last 32 and then likely the winner of Group E - Germany perhaps in the last 16.  Whereas Spain, if they win their group, play 2nd place J (Algeria/Austria)  and then the winner of 2nd L and 2nd K - Colombia or Croatia maybe.  Argentina, Netherlands and Brazil are the other 3 teams that won't play a group winner until the quarter finals.  Obviously there will random results and surprises but seems to be a slightly eaiser route for  those 4 teams. In the 32 team World Cups each group winner played a group runner up in the last 16 so it was uniform.

The biggest World Cup ever, but where are all the big games? In truth, this has long been a problem with the World Cup, but it seems especially stark that in a World Cup with 48 teams they have contrived to produce so few big games ahead of the knockout stages. That’s not to say there won’t be \*exciting\* games as such, but for the first 72 games of football’s premier event to look so… meh on paper feels sad.  Firstly, what is a big game? Let’s adopt a fairy loose definition: a big game is hereby defined as a game where both participants have made the WC semi-final at least twice since 1970. That encompasses every World Cup winner plus a decent number more.   How many big games does that make?  2. That’s it, out of 72 games. 2.7%  They are:  Spain vs Uruguay  England vs Croatia  As a point of comparison, by the same criteria, Euro 2024 had 6 out of 36 games:  Spain v Italy  Spain v Croatia  Croatia v Spain  France v Netherlands  Netherlands v Poland  Poland v France  Maybe I’m being harsh, but besides games featuring my own team there seem to be precious few games in the group stage that look genuinely interesting to me. There are one or two that look interesting for reasons unrelated to the on-pitch product (Mexico vs South Africa for instance), but I want to see classic World Cup ties between the best teams. Doubtless we’ll get them eventually in the knockouts, but it’s still a shame.   P.S. I’m not blind to the fact that this is an unavoidable consequence of seeding, but in truth that just goes to show how expanding the World Cup dilutes the competitiveness of the tournament.

Group placement and avoiding powerhouse teams in subsequent rounds One of the most interesting takes on the expanded World Cup that I have noticed and wonder about is how teams will view their group placement and the opponents in subsequent rounds. I’ve complied a list of groups where we can have unique scenarios on the final day of group matches.  We’ll start off the list with teams who may not be giving any thought to the matter and we’ll end the list with teams who may want to reconsider where they place.  *Disclosure: These scenarios only matter if the teams in question are positioned well enough to advance as top two prior to the final day of group stage matches.*  **Group F**  🇳🇱 Netherlands  🇯🇵 Japan  🇸🇪 Sweden  🇹🇳 Tunisia  The top teams of Group F and Group C will face each other in the Round of 32. On the final day of group matches, Group F will know beforehand who they face in the next round depending where they place.  This can play out uniquely on the final day of group F matches if a team wants to avoid a certain Group C team (like 🇧🇷Braz**i**l **o**r 🇲🇦Morocco)  **Group B**  🇨🇦 Canada  🇧🇦 Bosnia  🇶🇦 Qatar  🇨🇭 Switzerland  Placing first grants an easier Ro32 opponent (3rd best), but there is a strong possibility of facing 🇵**🇹P**ortugal in the Round of 16, which in many circles is considered a semi-finalist team.  Placing second grants a tough road, but not an impossible one, against a Ro32 Group A opponent and a Ro16 Group C or F opponent.  This could all be an unconcerning matter for a team like **Canada** because finishing first grants them home advantage.  **Group E**  🇩🇪 Germany  🇨🇼 Curaçao  🇨🇮 Ivory Coast  🇪🇨 Ecuador  Placing first grants an easier Ro32 opponent (3rd best), but there is a strong possibility of facing 🇫🇷France in the Ro16, which many people list as favorites to lift the trophy.  Placing second grants a tough road against a Ro32 Group 2I opponent and a Ro16 opponent from Group C or F.  Teams in Group E may reconsider finishing first as to avoid a team like **France** in the Ro16 and hedge their bets against the likes of 2I teams in the Ro32 (likely 🇸**🇳**Seneg**a**l or 🇳🇴Norway)  **Group J**  🇦🇷 Argentina  🇩🇿 Algeria  🇦🇹 Austria  🇯🇴 Jordan  The top teams of Group H and Group J will face each other in the Ro32. On the final day of group stage matches, Group J teams will know beforehand who they face in the next round depending where they place.  For example if 🇪🇸Spain, who is considered one of the favorites, finishes second in their group, we can see a scenario where Group J teams would reconsider finishing first and therefore play their last group games to try and finish second.  **TLDR:**  A unique final day of Group F matches where teams will want to avoid certain Group C teams in the Ro32.  A unique final day of Group B matches where teams will want to avoid a path toward Portugal in the Ro16.  A unique final day of Group E matches where teams will want to avoid a path toward France in the Ro16.  A unique final day of Group J matches where teams will want to avoid a second placed Spain in the Ro32.

Semi final spot 2: Spain will face either Croatia or Colombia, while two of the easiest groups with Turkey and Belgium as favourites only will meet one of them in the quarter final. Semi final spot 3: This is another outsider chance as Morocco (or Brazil), Japan and Norway will fight for the chance to meet England.   And yeah its impossible to guess which way this one will go.
